Article Title: Cabinet may clear Rs 10,000 crore SME growth fund, integrated logistics authority
Article Text:
Cabinet may clear Rs 10,000 crore SME growth fund, integrated logistics authority

NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet is likely to take up two proposals linked to the government’s growth and infrastructure priorities, including the setting up of an Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority and the Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.The SME (Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises) Growth Fund was announced by finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman as part of the government’s plan to strengthen the micro, small and medium enterprise (MSME) sector and help businesses emerge as future “Champions”.The fund is aimed at providing equity support to enterprises, with incentives linked to select criteria. Sitharaman had proposed the fund under the first of the government’s three ‘kartavya,’ accelerating and sustaining economic growth by improving productivity and competitiveness and building resilience to volatile global dynamics.The government had also proposed an additional Rs 2,000 crore for the Self-Reliant India Fund, which was set up in 2021. The additional allocation is intended to continue support for micro enterprises and maintain their access to risk capital.The Budget had outlined measures for MSMEs across three areas: equity, liquidity and professional support.On liquidity, Sitharaman said more than Rs 7 lakh crore had been made available to MSMEs through the Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS).She proposed making TReDS the transaction settlement platform for purchases from MSMEs by central public sector enterprises, introducing a credit guarantee mechanism through CGTMSE for invoice discounting on the platform, and linking GeM with TReDS to share information on government purchases with financiers.The government also proposed allowing TReDS receivables to be introduced as asset-backed securities to facilitate the development of a secondary market and improve liquidity and settlement of transactions.For professional support, the Budget proposed involving institutions such as ICAI, ICSI and ICMAI in developing short-term modular courses and practical tools to create a cadre of ‘Corporate Mitras’, particularly in Tier-II and Tier-III towns. These accredited para-professionals would help MSMEs meet compliance requirements at affordable costs.Sitharaman, while presenting the Budget, said that the Centre, “decisively and consistently chose action over ambivalence, reform over rhetoric and people over populism”.She said the government was guided by three ‘kartavya’, with the first focused on accelerating and sustaining economic growth.
Article Summary: The Union Cabinet is likely to take up two proposals linked to the government’s growth and infrastructure priorities. These include the setting up of an Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority and the Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund announced in the Union Budget 2026-27.

Article Title: Amazon Prime becomes 'permanent home' for Emmy Awards as 'Wheel Deal' system ends
Article Text:
Emmys shift from 'Wheel Deal' to Amazon Prime

The Emmys are leaving their decades-old broadcast TV rotation behind, with Amazon’s Prime Video set to become the awards show’s exclusive global streaming home from 2027.The Television Academy and Amazon announced a six-year agreement on Tuesday that will make the ceremony available live and free to audiences in more than 240 countries and territories. Furthermore, viewers will not need a Prime Video subscription to watch the show.The ceremony will continue to take place in September, with Prime Video’s rights beginning with the 2027 edition. NBC, owned by Comcast, aired this year’s ceremony on September 14.The deal brings an end to the “Wheel Deal” system under which ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC took turns broadcasting the Emmys. The arrangement has been in place since at least 1994, with the latest eight-year contract expiring this year.Prime Video has been named the “permanent home” of the Emmys in the announcement, marking a departure from the awards show’s long-running practice of moving between the four US broadcast networks.“Television has never been more global, and the Emmys should be a celebration that the world can share,” Television Academy chair Cris Abrego said in a statement.“Having a dedicated home with Prime Video allows us to build on that legacy with unprecedented global reach and a broader commitment to the Television Academy and our mission throughout the year,” he said.The financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed.The move comes as streaming services take a larger role in live television, while traditional broadcast and cable networks face increasing competition as viewing habits shift towards streaming subscriptions. Major entertainment and sports events have increasingly moved to or added streaming platforms, including events whose rights were previously held exclusively by traditional networks.The Emmys' move is also part of a wider shift among major US awards shows. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences announced in December 2025 that Alphabet’s YouTube and YouTube TV would take over media rights to the Oscars from ABC in 2029. Netflix has exclusively aired the SAG Awards since 2024.For Amazon, the agreement adds a major live entertainment event to Prime Video’s existing offering of original films and television programmes, sports and other streaming partnerships.First held in 1949, the Emmy Awards recognise achievements in television acting, production and writing, among other categories. The ceremony has traditionally been a major promotional and cultural event for the US television industry.
Article Summary: The Emmys are leaving their decades-old broadcast TV rotation behind. Amazon's Prime Video will become the awards show's exclusive global streaming home from 2027. The deal brings an end to the “Wheel Deal’ system under which ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC took turns broadcasting the Emmys.

Article Title: Starlink gets India-ready with 20 gateway sites, local data controls
Article Text:
Starlink

Starlink has completed a major ground infrastructure in India, with 20 gateway sites and hundreds of antennas already in place as the satellite communications company prepares to serve the Indian market.Lauren Dreyer, vice president, Starlink business operations, SpaceX , said at India Mobile Congress 2026 that the company has also developed security controls specifically for the country and is “keeping Indian users’ data within India.”Starlink has been working with regulators, industry stakeholders and operators for the past five years in India to align its operations with the country’s requirements. The government has granted licences to three satellite communication companies, including Starlink, to offer services in India.“We've built our Starlink operations specifically for India in recognition of Indian security requirements and other regulations, establishing controls at every layer for India, and keeping Indian user data within India,” Dreyer said.The company has already made investments in its ground network and established the operations needed to begin serving the market."We've already made the investment and built the existing ground infrastructure here, 20 gateway sites comprising hundreds of antennas, and we've established the operations to be ready to serve India," Dreyer said.Dreyer also pointed to the country's digital progress, saying, “What India has achieved digitally is extraordinary.”At the event, she also outlined SpaceX's broader technology work, including the development of reusable Falcon 9 rockets, the next-generation Starship launch vehicle and plans to build AI computing capacity at large scale.“With Falcon 9, reusable rockets at scale became reality, and we've baked all of that learning into the next generation Starship launch vehicle, which, of course, just reached orbit,” she said.SpaceX is also working on AI computing capacity on Earth and plans to build it in orbit in the future, Dreyer said.“With SpaceX AI, we're building AI compute at enormous scale, first here on Earth and in the future in orbit to fully harness the power of the sun…and Starlink is providing high-speed connectivity to places traditional infrastructure has been unable to reach and serve,” she said.
Article Summary: Starlink has completed a major ground infrastructure in India, with 20 gateway sites and hundreds of antennas already in place. The company has also developed security controls specifically for the country and is “keeping Indian users’ data within India”

Article Title: ‘Rate cuts off the table’: Why RBI hiked repo rate by 25 basis points but also raised GDP growth forecast to 7.1%
Article Text:
The MPC observed that geopolitical developments continue to make the global environment difficult.

Why RBI hiked repo rate by 25 basis points

RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra announced the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) decision to hike repo rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday. Repo rate is the rate at which RBI lends money to banks and it now stands at 5.50%. The rate hike by RBI follows a similar increase by the US Federal Reserve last month as global inflationary pressures prompt central banks to tighten liquidity.“The sudden reescalation of the West Asia conflict in September and the consequent hardening and volatility in global crude prices soured global economic sentiments and heightened financial market volatility. Although global growth remains resilient, it is projected to decelerate in 2026 from the previous year,” Sanjay Malhotra said.But amid all the global uncertainty, India’s growth remains strong, the central bank noted.Also Check | RBI MPC Meeting October 2026 Live Updates: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra announces 25 bps repo rate hike; your EMIs set to go up Two factors worked to decide MPC’s move: inflationary pressures persist and growth is beating estimates. Hence, a hike in repo rate, while helping keep inflation in check, is unlikely to substantially impact GDP growth.The MPC observed that geopolitical developments continue to make the global environment difficult.But, despite these external challenges, the Indian economy has remained robust, with growth momentum spread across various segments. The committee expects the economy to retain its resilience.In fact, the RBI has raised the real GDP growth forecast for the current financial year from 6.7% to 7.1% reflecting the confidence in the growth story.But inflation is a different story.The available data indicates that the inflation situation and its outlook are less favourable than they were last year. Headline CPI inflation is projected to average nearly 5.8% over the next three quarters, while core inflation is expected to average 4.4% during the current year. Against this backdrop, the MPC considered a recalibration of the policy rate necessary.When inflation originates from supply-side factors, monetary policy mainly works by containing the second-round impact, including changes in inflation expectations and pricing behaviour at the firm level. Such effects take time to emerge and can be difficult to identify separately from the available data, the MPC noted in its statement.There is some evidence that inflation expectations have risen and that price pressures are becoming more widespread. However, there are only limited indications that supply-side inflationary pressures have become firmly embedded in the pricing behaviour of firms.Likewise, there is limited evidence of demand-driven inflationary pressures at present. However, the strong expansion in monetary and credit aggregates creates risks that also need to be taken into account.RBI has raised its inflation forecast for financial year 2026-27 from 5% earlier to 5.2%.“The near-term outlook on inflation points towards continued pressures from the supply side, on account of the deficient Southwest monsoon, El Nino conditions and high volatility in international oil prices,” RBI governor said.“Price pressures are increasingly becoming visible across a range of commodities within the food component, apart from oil. In addition, early signs of inflation becoming generalised are also evident from the increase in core inflation and higher inflation across a larger segment of the CPI basket,” he added.After considering these factors, the MPC unanimously decided to raise the policy repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. It also changed its policy stance to calibrated tightening.“It only signals that given the current conditions, rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook,” the MPC statement said.The length and magnitude of the rate-hike cycle will depend on how growth and inflation actually develop and how their outlook changes.Particular attention will be paid to underlying inflation, the extent to which price pressures spread more broadly, the emergence of second-round effects from the supply shock, and the influence of demand impulses.
Article Summary: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra announced the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) decision to hike repo rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday. The rate hike by RBI follows a similar increase by the US Federal Reserve last month as global inflationary pressures prompt central banks to tighten liquidity.

Article Title: Man opted for VRS after employer shut plant, got Rs 65.21 lakh and reported it as advance salary in ITR; Section 89 relief was denied, but ITAT Pune later ruled it a non-taxable capital receipt
Article Text:
He reported the Rs 65.21 lakh as advance salary in his ITR and sought tax relief under Section 89 of the Income Tax Act. (Image for representative purpose only)

What the case is about

Why did the man win the case in ITAT?

You choose to retire early and get money from your company for the VRS. But you mistakenly report it in a wrong way in your income tax return. What happens then?In one such case a man chose to retire under a voluntary retirement scheme (VRS) following the closure of the manufacturing plant operated by his employer. The manner in which he initially disclosed this amount in his income tax return (ITR), however, led to a prolonged dispute with the Income Tax Department. He eventually won relief at the ITAT level.The man had been employed in Aurangabad. During FY 2018-19, his employer shut down its Aurangabad plant and introduced a financial scheme for its employees.Also Read | Homebuyer paid Rs 91 lakh upfront for a Rs 1.24 crore property, but circle value rose to Rs 1.46 crore by registration; why ITAT Kolkata gave her tax relief and deleted Rs 11.35 lakh addition The man opted for voluntary retirement under the scheme and received a total payment of Rs 65,21,105. The amount consisted of ex-gratia/severance pay, early bid and group participation incentives, and payment towards the notice period.He reported the Rs 65.21 lakh as advance salary in his ITR and sought tax relief under Section 89 of the Income Tax Act. Since the department considered this reporting incorrect, it rejected the relief claimed by him.During the subsequent proceedings, the man put forward a different legal argument.He contended that the amount could not be treated as salary in the first place. According to him, it was a capital receipt arising from the loss of his employment and was therefore not taxable.The matter then went before the CIT(A)/NFAC, which took the view that the amount was taxable as “Income from Other Sources” under Section 56(2)(xi). The appellate authority reached this conclusion on the basis that the payment had been received in connection with the termination of employment.The dispute over the correct character of the payment ultimately came before the Pune Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT).In its ruling dated June 8, 2026, the Pune ITAT accepted the man’s argument and held that the Rs 65.21 lakh constituted a non-taxable capital receipt.Chartered Accountant Suresh Surana explained to ET that the Pune ITAT, while deciding the case for AY 2019-20, allowed the appeal. The Tribunal held that the amount he received was a capital receipt and therefore was not chargeable to tax.The Pune ITAT consequently overturned the order passed by the CIT(A)/NFAC and directed the Assessing Officer to revise the assessment accordingly.Before the Pune ITAT, the man argued that the payment had arisen from his decision to take voluntary retirement/resignation under a special scheme and was not a payment made as a consequence of termination of his employment by the employer.Also Read | Tax raid finds Rs 1.12 crore cash and Rs 4.34 lakh foreign currency at Delhi man's home; he fights case twice, sister-in-law's explanation helps brother-in-law win ITAT battle He also referred to several earlier decisions of the Pune Tribunal involving other employees of the same company who were similarly placed. In those cases, payments received under the same scheme had been treated as capital receipts and held to be not chargeable to tax.Another argument advanced by the man was that Section 56(2)(xi) would apply only when compensation or another payment was received in connection with termination of employment or a modification in the terms of employment.The scheme, however, specifically stated that cessation of employment under the scheme would be treated as resignation and not as retrenchment or termination by the company.The Pune ITAT accepted this argument. It noted that under the relevant clause of the scheme, employees choosing voluntary retirement were not entitled to compensation or notice pay under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947.Their cessation from employment was expressly characterised as resignation rather than retrenchment or termination by the company.The Tribunal therefore concluded that Section 56(2)(xi) could not be invoked because the amount had not been received in connection with termination of employment.According to Surana, the Pune ITAT also applied the principle of consistency. The Tribunal noted that, in several cases involving other employees of the same company who had received similar payments under the same scheme, the Income Tax Department had accepted the receipts as capital in nature during reassessment proceedings. Various co-ordinate benches of ITATs had also ruled in favour of similarly placed employees.The Pune ITAT held that the lower authorities had not followed the applicable precedent and had failed to maintain consistency despite the factual circumstances being identical.Thus, the man succeeded because the Tribunal found that the payment arose from voluntary retirement/resignation rather than termination of employment. The amount was treated as a capital receipt arising from the loss of employment/source of income. Section 56(2)(xi) was therefore held to be inapplicable, while earlier co-ordinate bench decisions involving similarly placed Pfizer employees also supported his position.The appeal was accordingly allowed in favour of the assessee.Also Read | He left his BMW locked on the highway after midnight puncture, next morning it was found burnt; insurer rejected claim, but consumer commission orders Rs 70 lakh plus 7% interest
Article Summary: A man chose to retire under a voluntary retirement scheme (VRS) following the closure of the manufacturing plant operated by his employer. He reported the Rs 65.21 lakh as advance salary in his ITR and sought tax relief under Section 89 of the Income Tax Act. The Income Tax Department considered this reporting incorrect and rejected the relief claimed by him. He eventually won relief at the ITAT level.

Article Title: RBI raises interest rates, hikes FY27 growth forecast by 40bps and inflation by 20bps
Article Text:
RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra announces raising repo rates by 25 basis points

Follow live updates here:

RBI hikes repo rate for first time since February 2023

MUMBAI: The RBI raised the repo rate by a widely expected 25 basis points to 5.50% on Wednesday as stronger-than-expected growth and broader price pressures prompted the Monetary Policy Committee to unanimously vote for a hike and shift its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening.The move will raise the EMI on a Rs 1 crore loan over 15 years by around Rs 1,500 a month, or about Rs 1,471 at a base rate of 8.50%. If the EMI remains unchanged, the higher rate could extend the loan by about 5.5 to 5.9 months, equivalent to six additional instalments. The rate hike is good news for savers and retired individuals living on fixed income. Bajaj Finance has been the first to announce a 15 to 40 bps increase in fixed deposit rates following the RBI decision.The RBI raised its FY27 real GDP growth forecast by 40 basis points from the August review to 7.1%, driven largely by a sharp revision in Q2 growth to 7.2% from 6.4%. The Q3 forecast was also raised while the Q4 projection was unchanged.The FY27 inflation forecast was raised by 20 basis points to 5.2%. All quarterly forecasts provided for comparison were revised higher, with the largest increase being the 30-basis-point rise in the Q1 FY28 forecast to 5.6%, while the core inflation forecast was raised to 4.4%.RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra said that strong capacity utilisation, healthy bank credit growth and the central government's continued capital expenditure and infrastructure push were supporting investment. Double-digit growth in merchandise exports, buoyant services trade and bilateral trade agreements were also supporting aggregate demand.CPI inflation rose to 4.8% in Aug from 4.5% in July. Malhotra said price increases had broadened beyond volatile items, with food inflation becoming more widespread, including increases in sugar and onion.He said the change in stance meant rate cuts were no longer the likely next move. "Given the current conditions, rate cuts are off the table in the near term and policy action ahead can only be a rate hike or a pause, depending on the evolving conditions and the outlook,” he said.The MPC expects headline CPI inflation to average nearly 5.8% over the subsequent three quarters. Malhotra said the inflation outlook had changed from a year earlier. "In the light of available data, it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year... In this milieu, recalibrating the policy rate is imperative," he said.Headline CPI inflation is projected at 5.2% for FY27, peaking at 6.0% in Q3 before easing to 5.7% in Q4 and 5.6% in Q1 FY28.Deficient southwest monsoon rainfall and prevailing El Niño conditions pose risks to agricultural output. Renewed conflict in West Asia has increased crude oil price volatility, keeping energy and other input costs elevated.The indirect pass-through of commodity and energy costs is unfolding alongside upside risks from rapid growth in domestic monetary and credit aggregates.Malhotra said the indicators did not allow the RBI to cleanly separate second-round effects from supply pressures. "It may, however, be kept in mind that it is difficult to distinguish between the second-round effects and the indirect impact of supply side pressures (in production cost through energy and other inputs) as both are present in these indicators," he said.The RBI also cited tighter global financial conditions, US Federal Reserve rate hikes, high global bond yields and geopolitical instability in West Asia as external risks. It said India's external sector provided buffers against these pressures through steady capital inflows, remittances, services exports, a recovery in merchandise trade and foreign exchange reserves.
Article Summary: The move will raise the EMI on a Rs 1 crore loan over 15 years by around Rs 1,500 a month. The rate hike is good news for savers and retired individuals living on fixed income. Bajaj Finance has been the first to announce a 15 to 40 bps increase in fixed deposit rates.

Article Title: Cabinet OKs 10,000 crore SME growth fund
Article Text:
Centre approves Rs 10,000 crore fund for equity capital of SME as FTAs open expansion opportunities

NEW DELHI: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the setting up of Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund (SGF), aimed at catalysing growth-oriented capital for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to enable the emergence of champion enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains. The fund was announced in the last budget, focusing on providing equity, liquidity and professional support for the MSME ecosystem."There are existing funds which provide equity support but majority of them focus on early-stage enterprises and cover majorly micro enterprises. A structural gap exists for equity growth capital for SMEs. The fund will consider SME's operating in industrial clusters in Tier II and Tier III cities," government said in a statement. It added that by providing long-term capital, the initiative will enable Indian SMEs to scale operations.
Article Summary: The Union Cabinet on Tuesday approved the setting up of Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund (SGF) The fund is aimed at catalysing growth-oriented capital for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) It will enable emergence of champion enterprises across manufacturing, services, technology, innovation-driven sectors and strategic value chains.

Article Title: 4G mobiles make a comeback on costlier 5G smartphones
Article Text:
Smartphone prices (Image for representation)

NEW DELHI: Costlier smartphones are slowing India's shift to 5G. Rising component costs are driving a comeback for 4G devices as buyers seek better specifications at affordable prices.Shipments of 4G smartphones are expected to grow 3% in 2026 even as the overall market declines, according to Counterpoint Research. Their share of smartphone shipments is projected to rise from 11% in 2025 to 13% this year and 15% in 2027.The shift is particularly visible in the Rs 10,000-20,000 segment, where the number of smartphone makers offering 4G models has increased from two in 2025 to 12 this year. "India's 4G recovery is increasingly extending beyond the traditional entry-level segment," Counterpoint senior analyst Prachir Singh said. Buyers in this price band are seeking better device experiences without the higher price associated with 5G, he added.India's overall smartphone shipments fell 11% year-on-year in the June quarter, Counterpoint said, with record-high memory costs triggering multiple price hikes and weakening demand, particularly at the lower end."Building a 5G phone under Rs 15,000 that doesn't compromise on the overall experience has become extremely challenging," Sumit Singh, SVP and head of products at Lava International, told TOI."At the same time, consumer purchasing power hasn't grown to match these rising costs."Lava continues to prioritise 5G but has revisited its strategy for the sub-Rs 15,000 market. Demand, Singh said, is "not for the cheapest phone" but for better value, specifications and ownership experience. Brands like Xiaomi, Infinix, Realme have also launched 4G phones this year.Counterpoint research director Tarun Pathak said the shift could outlast a temporary response to higher prices because component costs are unlikely to normalise quickly. For manufacturers, this creates room to offer better-equipped 4G devices at affordable prices, while buyers increasingly weigh connectivity against the overall experience. The trade-off is making 4G a broader value proposition beyond its traditional entry-level role.
Article Summary: Shipments of 4G smartphones are expected to grow 3% in 2026 even as the overall market declines. The shift is particularly visible in the Rs 10,000-20,000 segment. India's overall smartphone shipments fell 11% year-on-year in the June quarter.

Article Title: Volatility triggered by CAS surges on NSE on expiry day
Article Text:
Representative image

MUMBAI: After a break of about two weeks, Closing Auction Session (CAS) again played truant during Tuesday's late session as weekly derivatives contracts on NSE were expiring. Within a span of just 30 seconds-between 15:20:00 and 15:20:30-Nifty rallied a little over 300 points or about 1.5%, and in the next eight minutes fell about 240 points or 1.1%. Sensex also saw a sudden spike but a relatively smaller one during CAS. The index rose about 350 points or 0.5% and then fell from the high. To address issues of CAS-related volatility, markets regulator Sebi is working on changing some rules for the session.At the close of Tuesday's trading, sensex was up 685 points or 1% while Nifty closed 220 points or 1% up at 22,776 points. The gains in the indices, which marked the second consecutive day of rise, came on the back of falling Brent prices that went below the psychologically important $100/barrel level, along with strong global cues.According to Vinod Nair, head of research, at Geojit Investments, crude oil prices slipped below the $100-mark after a large G7 stockpile release and alternative supply measures helped offset disruptions to vessel movements through the Strait of Hormuz."Coupled with strong Q2 business updates from financials and retail along with supportive global cues, the decline in oil prices improved investors' sentiment and supported a rebound from the oversold levels.Domestically, attention now shifts to the Q2 earnings season for silver lining amid weak sequential expectations due to elevated input costs," Nair wrote in a note to investors.Market players said Dalal Street investors would remain cautious ahead of the RBI policy decision on Wednesday, "with the focus firmly on the central bank's inflation outlook and guidance on further policy tightening," Nair said.Interestingly, the day's gains in the two indices came despite Rs 2,961 crore worth of net selling by foreign funds in the stock market, BSE data showed. In contrast, domestic institutions were net buyers at Rs 5,089 crore.
Article Summary: After a break of about two weeks, Closing Auction Session (CAS) again played truant during Tuesday's late session. Within a span of just 30 seconds, Nifty rallied a little over 300 points or about 1.5%, and in the next eight minutes fell about 240 points or 1.1%. Sensex also saw a sudden spike but a relatively smaller one during CAS.

Article Title: World Bank raises India's FY27 growth forecast to 7.1%
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: The Indian economy is expected to grow 7.1% in 2026-27, against 6.6% estimated earlier, on the back of strong domestic demand and exports, despite global headwinds, the World Bank said Tuesday.The multilateral agency is the latest to revise its projections after India's growth accelerated to 7.8% during the first quarter of the current financial year, prompting upgrades from ADB, S&P, Moody's and other global entities, which typically take a cue from official data. In 2027-28, the World Bank expects the Indian economy to grow by 7.2%."Medium term prospects are strong, but external risks are elevated, including downside risks related to global oil prices, El Nino and stock market corrections that would result in capital flow volatility," World Bank said in a statement.It expects the "strong" momentum in industry and services to continue, with the reforms that have been undertaken - consolidation of labour codes, GST reforms, tariff rationalisation , IBC amendments, and investments in physical and digital infrastructure. In the medium-term, growth is projected to average 7.1% between 2027-28 and 2028-29, with a narrowing current deficit and declining inflation."Strength in the rest of the economy is expected to make up for agricultural weakness," the World Bank said, adding that the sub-par monsoons will likely reduce agricultural output and rural demand, while increasing food inflation.This will add to existing pressure from higher energy prices.Besides, the biannual update said India is well positioned to harness AI, thanks to its large technical workforce, globally integrated IT sector, and digital public infrastructure. Currently, it is ranked 10th in AI readiness, behind the US (rank 1), China (2nd) and South Korea (6th).According to a survey by the global financial institution, 23.4% of Indian firms use some form of AI, compared with 42.7% of firms in the US. The gap widens considerably when the sophistication of AI use is considered.
Article Summary: The Indian economy is expected to grow 7.1% in 2026-27, against 6.6% estimated earlier. In 2027-28, the World Bank expects the Indian economy to grow by 7.2%. It expects the "strong" momentum in industry and services to continue.

Article Title: Nobel Prize Winners 2026: Meet Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel, winners of Medicine award
Article Text:
Nobel Prize in Medicine 2026: Meet Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel. (Illustrations: Inklas Elmehed)

Meet Karl Deisseroth

Meet Peter Hegemann

Meet Georg Nagel

How their work changed neuroscience

The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine has been awarded jointly to Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel for their discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics. The Nobel Assembly at Karolinska Institutet announced the award on October 5, 2026.The three scientists' work established the foundations of optogenetics, a method that allows researchers to control nerve cells using light and investigate how neural circuits influence memories, feelings and behaviour. The prize carries an award of 12 million Swedish kronor, which will be shared equally among the three laureates.Karl Deisseroth, born in 1971, is associated with the Howard Hughes Medical Institute and Stanford University in the US. He is the D.H. Chen Professor and Professor of Bioengineering and of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Stanford.Deisseroth earned his Ph.D. in 1998 and MD in 2000 from Stanford University. His contribution to the Nobel-recognised work came when he introduced the gene for channelrhodopsin into rat nerve cells.By exposing the modified cells to blue light, he demonstrated that nerve signals could be triggered.In 2007, he demonstrated that the light-controlled switch could also be used in the brains of living mice.Peter Hegemann, born in 1954, is Hertie Senior Professor of Neuroscience at Humboldt University of Berlin, Germany. He received his Ph.D. in 1984 from the Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry in Martinsried.Hegemann's research began with a question about how the single-celled alga Chlamydomonas moves towards light. His work led to the identification of channelrhodopsin, a protein that responds to blue light by opening a channel through which charged ions can flow.The prize-recognised discoveries were made at the Max Planck Institute for Biochemistry.Georg Nagel, born in 1953, is Professor of Molecular Plant Physiology at the University of Würzburg, Germany. He received his Ph.D. in 1988 from the University of Frankfurt.Nagel worked with Hegemann on channelrhodopsin, the light-sensitive protein found in Chlamydomonas. Their research showed that the protein could make other cells responsive to light.Nagel's prize-recognised discoveries were made at the Max Planck Institute for Biophysics in Frankfurt. The discoveries by Hegemann and Nagel provided the light-sensitive protein, while Deisseroth developed its use as a controllable switch in nerve cells. This approach became known as optogenetics.Researchers can use optogenetics to investigate neural circuits associated with specific memories, feelings and behaviours. The method is also being studied in clinical research, including attempts to restore sight in people with visual impairment.The Nobel Assembly said optogenetics has changed the study of the brain by enabling researchers to investigate relationships between nerve-cell activity and behaviour with greater precision.
Article Summary: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Their work established the foundations of optogenetics, a method that allows researchers to control nerve cells using light. The prize carries an award of 12 million Swedish kronor, which will be shared equally.

Article Title: Nandini milk price shocker: Karnataka clears Rs 8/litre hike, blue-packet toned milk may hit Rs 54
Article Text:
Nandini milk prices are expected to rise by up to Rs 8 per litre following government approval





BENGALURU: Nandini milk is set to become costlier by up to Rs 8 a litre, with the state Cabinet approving the hike on Tuesday but holding back its announcement because of the Model Code of Conduct for Legislative Council elections.The proposed increase would be the fifth revision in Nandini milk prices since November 2022. Prices were raised by Rs 3 in November 2022, Rs 3 in July 2023, Rs 2 in June 2024 and Rs 4 in March 2025.In June 2024, consumers were given an additional 50 ml for every litre, but KMF later withdrew the additional quantity.The government will seek Election Commission clearance before implementing the decision. The Cabinet has authorised Chief Minister DK Shivakumar to take the final call on the extent of the hike and its implementation.Ministers who attended the meeting said the revised prices are likely to take effect from November 1, subject to EC clearance.Under the proposal, Rs 6 of the Rs 8 increase will go to milk producers and Rs 2 to milk unions. If the entire hike is passed on to consumers, toned milk in the blue packet will cost Rs 54 a litre, up from Rs 46.“Due to the drought situation, farmers are facing crop losses and a shortage of fodder, among other problems.Protecting their interests is important for the government and hence the Cabinet approved the proposal to hike milk prices,” a minister said.The unions, which met Shivakumar, had recently sought a hike of Rs 8 to Rs 10 per litre, citing higher costs of cattle feed, fodder, medicines, transport and plastic packaging.They had also pointed to Karnataka’s lower procurement price compared with neighbouring states.According to the unions, toned milk is procured at Rs 35 a litre in Karnataka, against Rs 41.5 in Andhra Pradesh, Rs 41.8 in Kerala, Rs 41 in Maharashtra and Rs 42.2 in Tamil Nadu.Amul and Mother Dairy had in May raised milk prices by Rs 2 per litre from May 14, citing rising operational costs and inflation.
Article Summary: The proposed increase would be the fifth revision in Nandini milk prices since November 2022. The government will seek Election Commission clearance before implementing the decision. If the entire hike is passed on to consumers, toned milk in the blue packet will cost Rs 54 a litre.

Article Title: Francis Halzen wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics
Article Text:
Francis Halzen wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics (Credit: Academia Europaea)

The prize and the selection

Last year's winners

Other prizes this year

Chemistry, Wednesday:

Literature, Thursday:

Peace, Friday:

Economic Sciences, next Monday:

Award ceremony

Belgian-American particle physicist Francis Halzen has won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for "decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin". The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences announced the award on Tuesday.Halzen is a physics professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He was born in 1944 in Tienen, Belgium.The winners of the physics prize are selected by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences. The prize sum is 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million), which is shared among the winners if there are several.The Nobel Prizes were established under the will of Alfred Nobel, a Swedish inventor and entrepreneur whose fortune was built in part on the invention of dynamite. They were first awarded in 1901 and honour achievements in science, literature and peace. The economics award was added later by Sweden's central bank.Physics had a prominent place in Nobel's will, and the prize remains one of the discipline's highest distinctions. Past laureates include Albert Einstein, Marie and Pierre Curie, Max Planck and Niels Bohr.John Clarke, Michel Devoret and John Martinis shared the 2025 physics prize.The three are based in the United States. They were recognised for experiments that made the behaviour of the subatomic world observable in a system large enough to see with the naked eye. The research is seen as helping to advance the next generation of computing and other digital technologies.The physics award is the second of six Nobel Prizes this year. Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel won the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine on Monday. They were honoured for the discovery of a neuroscience tool that may one day lead to a treatment for blindness.The remaining announcements are scheduled as follows:The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences will announce the prize in Stockholm. Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson and Omar Yaghi won last year for developing molecular building blocks with spaces large enough for gases and other chemicals to flow through them.The Swedish Academy will announce the prize in Stockholm. Hungarian novelist Laszlo Krasznahorkai, known for dystopian themes and relentless prose, won last year.The Norwegian Nobel Institute will announce the prize in Oslo. Maria Corina Machado won last year after building a social movement in Venezuela that challenged the country's authoritarian president.The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences will announce the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in Stockholm. Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt won last year for research explaining the relationship between technological progress and sustained economic growth.All announcements are streamed live by the Nobel Prize organisation.King Carl XVI Gustaf of Sweden will present the Nobel medals at a ceremony in Stockholm on December 10, the anniversary of Alfred Nobel's death. A banquet at Stockholm City Hall follows the awards. The peace prize is the only Nobel not presented in Sweden and is awarded separately in Oslo.
Article Summary: Francis Halzen is a physics professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison. He was born in 1944 in Tienen, Belgium. The prize sum is 12 million Swedish crowns ($1.2 million) The physics award is the second of six Nobel Prizes this year.

Article Title: Brent crosses $101 as Saudi attacks, US storm add to oil supply concerns
Article Text:
Brent crosses $101 once again

Oil prices rose more than 1% on Wednesday, with Brent crude crossing the $101-a-barrel mark as fresh supply risks outweighed rising optimism due to increased Middle East crude supplies.WTI crude rose 1.05% to $90.38 a barrel, while Brent crude gained 1.02% to $101.60 as supply concerns emerged in Saudi Arabia and the US oil and refining sector.The latest concerns came from both sides of the global oil supply chain. According to US forecasters, a storm developing in the Gulf of Mexico is expected to become the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 within two days and is likely to affect oil and gas facilities.The areas in the storm's path account for 15% of US crude production and 5% of the country's natural gas production. Six refineries could also be affected. Refineries located in US Gulf states represent about 50% of the country's total refining capacity of 18.2 million barrels per day (bpd).The prospect of disruption has emerged even as oil supplies from the Middle East have increased. Saudi energy minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman on Tuesday said that supply had been rising, with the East-West pipeline reaching 5.8 million barrels a day.The head of Vitol said that around 12 million barrels per day of crude oil and 2 million bpd of refined products had been shipped out of the Middle East by tankers over the previous seven to 10 days.US inventory data, however, offered a mixed picture. According to market sources citing by Reuters, crude and gasoline inventories declined last week, while distillate stocks increased marginally. US crude inventories fell by 2.09 million barrels in the week ended October 2.Meanwhile, tensions around Saudi Arabia have added another risk to regional supply. The Saudi aviation authority said airports in Jazan and Najran were attacked twice on Monday evening as hostilities between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis escalated.The attacks came as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces pursued a major offensive to regain territory from the Houthis after weeks of rebel advances. Saudi Arabia has increased airstrikes in support of the campaign.Mukesh Sahdev, chief oil analyst at X Analysts in Sydney, said the attacks and refinery outages could continue to support higher oil prices.“Attacks and refinery outages are likely to keep the cracks elevated and scarcity will transmit to crude. Prices will stay elevated near a $100 level without any material de-escalation emerging,” Sahdev said.The wider tensions involving Iran have also remained unresolved. US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that there was uncertainty over who was running Iran during the eight-month US-Israeli war with Iran."Their leaders are gone, their second group of leaders are gone, and the biggest problem I have is nobody knows who the hell is running the country," Trump said.Iran's foreign ministry spokesman said on Sunday that Washington knows very well who its counterpart is in Iran and how the decision-making system in the country works.
Article Summary: WTI crude rose 1.05% to $90.38 a barrel, while Brent crude gained 1.02% to £101.60. Fresh supply concerns emerged in Saudi Arabia and the US oil and refining sector. A storm developing in the Gulf of Mexico is expected to become the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026 within two days.

Article Title: Wall Street today: US stocks nears record highs amid earnings optimism, tech rally; S&P, Nasdaq rise 0.8%
Article Text:
Dow, S&P, Nasdaq rise to near record highs

Software stocks stage a comeback

US stocks moved closer to record highs on Tuesday, helped by stronger earnings expectations, easing oil prices and a renewed rally in technology shares.The S&P 500 rose 0.8 per cent and was on course to close above its previous record set in August. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 343 points, or 0.7 per cent, while the Nasdaq Composite added 0.8%, moving towards a fresh record after reaching an all-time high a day earlier.The gains have come despite continued concerns over inflation, elevated bond yields and the economic impact of the war with Iran. The S&P 500 has risen nearly 24% since hitting its low in late March.A key support for the rally has been expectations of stronger corporate profits. Analysts expect companies in the S&P 500 to report nearly 30% growth in earnings per share for the July-September quarter, according to FactSet. If realised, it would mark the third consecutive quarter in which earnings growth exceeded 25%.The easing in oil prices also provided some relief. Brent crude fell 1.1% to $99.19 a barrel, down from nearly $110 a few weeks ago. The decline helped push the yield on the 10-year US Treasury note down to 5.26%, from 5.31% on Monday.US software stocks have emerged as another driver of the market's recent strength, with investors increasingly betting that artificial intelligence will help rather than destroy demand for many software companies.The S&P 500 software and services index rose 1.3 per cent on Tuesday to its highest level since November 2025. The index also recorded its strongest quarterly gain since the second quarter of 2020 during the July-September period.Companies including Salesforce, ServiceNow and Accenture have reported strong results, while partnerships with AI companies have helped improve sentiment towards the sector. Cybersecurity stocks have performed particularly strongly as businesses increase spending to protect systems in the age of AI.CrowdStrike, Fortinet and Palo Alto Networks have all recorded triple-digit gains this year.“AI has been more of an enabler for a lot of these software companies, more than a disruptor,” said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist at LPL Financial.The software index is up about 5% this year, while the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index has surged 87.5%, although chip stocks have pulled back from their highs. Meanwhile, expectations for software-sector earnings growth in 2026 have climbed to 20.6%, from 13.8% at the end of March, according to LSEG data.Software stocks suffered a sharp selloff earlier this year, with the sector falling more than 26% from late January to its April low. The decline was driven by fears that companies could use AI to develop software internally at a much lower cost, threatening traditional software providers.Those concerns now appear to have eased as companies report continued demand and greater adoption of AI tools.“The whole SaaSpocalypse didn't happen anywhere near as fast as some of the people on Wall Street thought it would,” said Rebecca Wettemann, CEO of technology research firm Valoir.However, analysts warn that AI remains a longer-term risk for the industry. Brian Mulberry, chief market strategist at Zacks Investment Management, said the more significant test for software companies could come in the second half of 2027, when greater data-centre capacity could make AI-powered coding a bigger challenge for traditional software businesses.Additionallly, several major companies are due to report results in the coming days. Delta Air Lines is scheduled to report third-quarter earnings on Friday, followed by several major US banks next week.In overseas markets, European stocks edged higher as investors continued to monitor government debt and bond yields. Japan's Nikkei 225 rose 1.1%, Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained 1%, while South Korea's Kospi fell 0.9%.
Article Summary: S&P 500 rose 0.8% and was on course to close above its previous record. Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 343 points, or 0.7%. Nasdaq Composite added 0. 8%, moving towards a fresh record. Gains come despite continued concerns over inflation, elevated bond yields and the economic impact of the war with Iran.

Article Title: Fueling both sides? South Korea ships 150,000T fuel to Russia while funding Ukraine
Article Text:
South Korea ships 150,000 tonnes fuel to Russia while funding Ukraine

Three sanctioned tankers sail to Russia

Russia turns to import fuel

South Korea is backing Ukraine, but its fuel tankers are sailing in the opposite direction — towards Russia.In July and August, more than 176,000 tonnes of fuel, mainly diesel, was shipped from South Korea to Russia as Moscow turned to imports to make up for falling domestic fuel production.The fuel was loaded at several South Korean ports and carried to Russia’s far east in 14 voyages by seven tankers, according to an analysis of port records and ship-tracking data by The Guardian. Three of the vessels were under UK and European Union sanctions.One sanctioned tanker received about 26,000 tonnes of fuel from another vessel in a ship-to-ship transfer in South Korean waters. Such transfers can make cargo origins harder to trace and allow ships to avoid port terminals.The largest carrier was the sanctioned Layla, which made two trips from Ulsan in south-eastern South Korea to Vladivostok on 19 July and 10 August, carrying 57,000 tonnes of diesel in total.On its first trip, Layla told South Korean authorities it was heading to Vladivostok. On the second, it declared Niigata in Japan as its destination before sailing to Vladivostok.The Russian-flagged Astoria, also under Australian sanctions, loaded nearly 11,000 tonnes of fuel at Ulsan on 1 August.It declared Japan as its destination before sailing to Vladivostok.The third sanctioned tanker, Chongchon, did not berth at a port. Instead, it took on about 26,000 tonnes of fuel from the unsanctioned Celeste I at an anchorage off Yeosu in southern South Korea in early August. It then sailed to Vladivostok after declaring Singapore as its destination.The owners and managers of the four tankers did not respond to requests for comment. South Korean port records do not show who owned or sold the fuel.The shipments come as Ukrainian drone strikes disrupt Russia’s oil-refining capacity.The International Energy Agency said Russian refinery throughput fell in June to its lowest level in more than 20 years. Diesel production was nearly 30% lower than a year earlier.Ukraine’s military intelligence agency, the HUR, has said Moscow has been forced to import fuel products to feed the “Russian war machine”.Russia imported 368,000 tonnes of oil products by sea in August, according to Kpler data analysed by CREA. That was more than seven times the previous month and the highest monthly total since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine.South Korea supplied 112,000 tonnes, or 31%, of the total, second only to India.Kpler data showed that buyers included Rosneft, Russia’s state-controlled oil company, which is under UK, US, EU and Australian sanctions. NNK, a Russian oil group, was also among the buyers. Its owner, Eduard Khudainatov, and NNK-Oil are under UK sanctions.South Korea balances Ukraine support with Russia tiesThe fuel trade comes despite South Korea’s support for Ukraine. Seoul has provided humanitarian aid and non-lethal military supplies, including helmets, body armour and demining vehicles. In 2023, it pledged $2.3bn in support, most of it in loans.President Lee Jae Myung also pledged $100m for Ukraine’s reconstruction at a Nato summit in Turkey.But Seoul has also sought to maintain ties with Russia. Throughout the war, it has ruled out sending weapons directly to Ukraine, in line with its policy of not supplying lethal arms to countries at war.Moscow has also shown interest in restoring relations with South Korea, including trade ties.The fuel shipments involve vessels sanctioned by some of South Korea’s western partners but do not appear to breach South Korean law. Seoul’s measures against Russia mainly focus on export controls covering goods such as industrial machinery, electronics and vehicles.The shipments come as relations between Seoul and Kyiv face strain over the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea, which Seoul has said was meant to remain secret.Seoul defends its export controlsFuel loadings at South Korean ports began to rise sharply in July, around the time Lee pledged $100m for Ukraine’s reconstruction.A 2025 trade association survey found that nearly 80% of South Korean companies that had stopped exporting to Russia since the war began were open to restarting trade.In March, South Korea capped exports of certain fuels and imported Russian naphtha under a US sanctions waiver after the war with Iran shut the Strait of Hormuz.On 1 October, the UK temporarily exempted South Korea’s existing gas contracts from a ban on maritime services for Russian LNG, which will take effect in January 2027.South Korea’s foreign ministry did not directly address the shipments or the sanctioned tankers. In a statement, it said that as “a responsible member of the international community, the government supports, and is actively taking part in, international efforts to help end the war in Ukraine and bring about a peaceful recovery.”The ministry said that it had expanded export controls on Russia under the Foreign Trade Act “beyond strategic items to 1,402 non-strategic items with a high potential for diversion to military use” and was “strictly enforcing” them.The government “continues to monitor the implementation of its export controls on Russia and, where necessary, takes action in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations,” the ministry said.
Article Summary: More than 176,000 tonnes of fuel, mainly diesel, was shipped from South Korea to Russia. Moscow turned to imports to make up for falling domestic fuel production. Fuel was loaded at several South Korean ports and carried to Russia’s far east in 14 voyages by seven tankers. Three of the vessels were under UK and EU sanctions.

Article Title: Google nears $1 billion-plus nuclear power deal with Constellation amid AI boom
Article Text:
Google to seal $1 billion-plus nuclear power

Why tech cos are turning to nuclear power?

Google is close to striking a deal to buy nuclear power from Constellation Energy Corp, for its data centres, as tech gaints look for more reliable electricity to support the rapid growth of artificial intelligence.The Alphabet Inc. company could pay $1 billion or more under a multi-year agreement with Constellation, according to people familiar with the talks, as cited by Bloomberg. The deal could be announced as soon as this week. The people asked not to be named because the discussions are private.The possible deal would add to the company's already existing agreements with nuclear power companies. Last year, Google agreed to buy electricity from NextEra Energy Inc. The deal will support the company's plans to restart the Duane Arnold reactor in Iowa, which has been shut since 2020.Google also reached an agreement with Southern Co. last month for new nuclear capacity by funding upgrades at two nuclear plants. The tech firm's talks with Constellation come as technology companies face rising electricity needs from the artificial intelligence boom and growing data-centre demand.Nuclear power can provide electricity around the clock and does not produce emissions. Recent deals have mainly focused on existing nuclear plants because building new reactors can take a decade or more, including the time needed for permits and construction.The next generation of nuclear technology is also still expected to be years away from being widely deployed.Amazon.com Inc. agreed last week to buy 690 megawatts of power from Constellation. The deal includes capacity from an upgrade to the Calvert Cliffs nuclear facility in Maryland, Bloomberg reported.Microsoft Corp. agreed in 2024 to buy power from the shut Three Mile Island nuclear plant in Pennsylvania, where Constellation is planning to restart the reactor by next year.Nuclear energy has gained interest again in recent years after safety concerns and high costs reduced interest in it earlier last decade.Growing demand for electricity from data centres has also increased interest in nuclear power. Apart from companies, many countries are also turning to nuclear energy to meet rising power demand while reducing emissions.
Article Summary: Google is close to striking a deal to buy nuclear power from Constellation Energy Corp, for its data centres. The company could pay $1 billion or more under a multi-year agreement with Constellation, according to people familiar with the talks. The deal could be announced as soon as this week.

Article Title: Saudi oil under fire, Aramco plots new routes to keep barrels flowing
Article Text:
Smoke rises from a fire at the Aramco refinery south of Riyadh (Reuters)

Saudi Aramco is working on new oil export routes and overseas storage as repeated attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure and tankers expose vulnerabilities in the kingdom’s crude supply network.According to Reuters, Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said the company is working on a fourth and fifth export route and studying additional overseas storage to help deal with short-term disruptions.He said Aramco is currently meeting all customer requirements and can make 12 million barrels per day available within days if needed."We start repairing assets while they are still on fire," Nasser said, describing Aramco’s approach to damaged infrastructure.Nasser said Aramco continues to export crude through Yanbu as well as Egypt’s Sidi Kerir and Port Said, while also relying heavily on ship-to-ship transfers to keep supplies moving.Looking beyond the immediate oil supply disruptions, Nasser also outlined Aramco's longer term plans for natural gas. He said the company expects to produce around 9 million barrels of oil equivalent per day of natural gas by 2040.The comments come amid escalating attacks by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebels on Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping.The attacks have raised concerns over the security of Saudi Arabia’s oil export network, particularly after disruptions to the East-West pipeline, a key route that allows the kingdom to move crude towards the Red Sea and bypass the Strait of Hormuz.Nasser also warned that commercially available information is making energy infrastructure easier to track and target."Open data such as satellite imagery and shipping logs are increasingly being weaponised against infrastructure and tankers," he said.Despite the attacks, Nasser said Aramco has not needed to tap its strategic product reserves and has enough inventory within its system to continue supplying customers.But the disruption is already creating a significant premium in the physical oil market. Nasser said physical barrels are sometimes trading $20 to $50 per barrel above the Brent benchmark, highlighting the rising cost of securing and transporting crude.The Aramco CEO also warned that the impact of the disruption could persist even after immediate supply routes stabilise. He said the world needs at least 2 million barrels per day of additional demand for the next 18 months to rebuild current oil inventories.Looking beyond the immediate oil disruption, Nasser also outlined Aramco's long-term gas ambitions, saying the company expects to produce around 9 million barrels of oil equivalent per day of natural gas by 2040.The 2040 target is part of Aramco's longer term strategy, separate from the immediate security challenges facing its oil export network.
Article Summary: Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said the company is working on a fourth and fifth export route and studying additional overseas storage. He said Aramco is currently meeting all customer requirements and can make 12 million barrels per day available within days if needed. Nasser also outlined Aramco's longer term plans for natural gas.

Article Title: Japan's Nikkei jumps 2.5% above 70,000 to three-month high as AI stocks rally
Article Text:
Japan's Nikkei rises to three month-high

Wall Street gains lift Japan stocks

30-year bond yield hits record high

What is keeping bond market under pressure

Japan’s Nikkei got an AI-powered boost on Monday, jumping over 2% to cross 70,000 for the first time in three months. Benchmark index Nikkei climbed 2.53% to 70,037.61 by the midday break, while the broader Topix gained 1.16% to 4,138.57.Chip-related companies emerged as the biggest drivers of Nikkei's rise. Tokyo Electron gained 5.7% and Advantest rose 4.5%, while technology investor SoftBank Group advanced 3.68%.Memory maker Kioxia, however, rose only 0.49%. Its shares remain nearly 50% below the record high reached in mid-June."Investors scooped up AI-related stocks, but the market sentiment is muted compared with earlier this year when the Nikkei hit a record high," said Mamoru Shimode, chief strategist at Resona Asset Management. The AI rally will continue, but the markets will be more selective."Shimode said Kioxia’s limited gains could reflect selling by investors who had suffered losses in the stock."Investors probably tried to buy Kioxia shares on the rise, but at the same time others who have losses in the shares sold stocks on a rally, which is why their gains are limited," Shimode said.The advance in Japanese equities followed a rise in US stocks on Friday.Weaker-than-expected jobs data reduced expectations for a rate hike by the Federal Reserve at its policy meeting this month.Japanese financial stocks also moved higher. Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group rose 0.99%, while Mizuho Financial Group gained 1.86%.Within the Topix, the growth share index climbed 1.46%, compared with a 0.89% rise in the value share index.The gains were mixed across the broader market. Of more than 1,500 stocks on the Tokyo Stock Exchange’s prime market, 53% rose, 42% declined and 3% were unchanged.While equities rallied, Japan’s bond market came under pressure, with the 30-year government bond yield climbing to a record 4.235%. The move came as investors awaited Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s policy speech later on Monday, which is being closely watched for clues on the government’s policy stance.Investors were awaiting Takaichi’s remarks at the opening of an extraordinary parliamentary session. Her policy speech is being closely watched after local media reported that she was expected to pledge a nimble response to unexpected developments in the economy and financial markets.Markets are also scrutinising her comments for signs of a possible shift in her reflationary policy stance, following US pressure to stem the yen’s weakness."The yields across the curve stand at this level based on expectations for a shift in Takaichi's policy, but if she says anything that could suggest she would keep her expansionary policy unchanged, that could send the bond yields higher," said Masahito Sugawara, a senior strategist at Daiwa Securities.Investors have become increasingly concerned that Takaichi’s ambitious spending plans could worsen Japan’s fiscal position. She took office a year ago, and the concerns have added pressure to the government bond market.The move was concentrated in longer-dated debt, while shorter-dated yields fell. The two-year JGB yield declined 1.5 basis points to 1.9%, while the 10-year bond yield dropped 2 basis points to 3.08%.The pressure on Japanese government bonds comes amid a broader sell-off in global government debt. Elevated energy prices, persistent inflation concerns and expectations of higher interest rates have pushed yields higher across global markets.US Treasury yields also reversed earlier declines over the weekend as investors assessed the weaker-than-expected September jobs report. The data tempered expectations for further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
Article Summary: Chip-related companies emerged as the biggest drivers of Nikkei's rise. The advance in Japanese equities followed a rise in US stocks on Friday. Japan’s bond market came under pressure, with the 30-year government bond yield climbing to a record 4.235%.

Article Title: Oil prices ease slightly as G7 and Middle East crude supplies set to hit market
Article Text:
Crude prices ease marginally on Monday

Oil prices found marginal relief on Monday as concerns over global energy supplies eased with more crude entering the market. Additional shipments from the Middle East, along with the Group of Seven’s decision to release oil from emergency reserves, helped offset concerns over possible further damage to energy infrastructure in the Gulf amid the Iran war.As of 7:15 am IST, Brent Crude was down 0.54% at $101.70 while WTI Crude fell 0.92% to $90.27.The G7 agreement to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency stocks came last week, following pressure from US President Donald Trump. The countries also pledged not to impose energy export restrictions.The G7 move comes as Middle Eastern crude exports have already picked up. Shipping data showed that exports were above pre-war levels on four of the seven days in the final week of September, despite attacks on vessels travelling through the Strait of Hormuz.The market remains exposed to developments around the Gulf.The Houthis said they had launched ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi Aramco sites in Riyadh and the Khurais area of Saudi Arabia, saying the attacks were in response to 50 Saudi-led air and missile strikes in Yemen over the previous 12 hours.Yemen's Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government said on Sunday that it was beginning a major military campaign to retake all areas of the country controlled by the Iran-backed Houthis.Aramco has also unexpectedly reduced its November crude oil prices for Asia to six-year lows, Reuters reported.Meanwhile, OPEC+ has postponed a review that was expected to determine oil output quotas for its members in 2027. Two sources close to the matter said the US-Israeli war on Iran had disrupted projects intended to expand production capacity across the Middle East, making estimates of future production potential uncertain.Developments in Europe are also shaping oil markets. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told Reuters that Ukraine would step up attacks on Russian oil refineries.Brent had surrendered most of its gains from the previous week, while WTI was 1.6% lower after the G7 decision.As the Middle East conflict stretches beyond the seven-month mark, the oil market has remained volatile. However, while prices have continued to rise broadly, the latest gains remain well below the spike seen earlier in the conflict, when crude touched $126 per barrel.
Article Summary: Brent Crude was down 0.54% at $101.70 while WTI Crude fell 0.92% to $90.27. G7 agreement to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency stocks came last week, following pressure from US President Donald Trump.

Article Title: OPEC+ keeps November oil output targets steady as Iran war hits supply
Article Text:
OPEC+ is closely monitoring developments in the oil market.

OPEC+ has agreed to keep its oil production targets unchanged for November, the group said in a statement after a meeting on Sunday, Reuters reported.The decision comes as the group continues to assess the impact of ongoing conflicts in West Asia and disruptions to oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz.OPEC+ had earlier decided to keep its production targets unchanged for October at a virtual meeting on September 6. The decision was taken by seven OPEC+ members, Saudi Arabia, Russia, Iraq, Kuwait, Kazakhstan, Algeria and Oman.The countries had earlier announced additional voluntary production adjustments in April and November 2023.The group is closely monitoring developments in the oil market as geopolitical tensions in West Asia continue to pose risks to supplies and exports.
Article Summary: OPEC+ has agreed to keep its oil production targets unchanged for November. Decision comes as the group continues to assess the impact of ongoing conflicts in West Asia and disruptions to oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz. The group is closely monitoring developments in the oil market as geopolitical tensions continue to pose risks to supplies and exports.

Article Title: US-Russia talks on Ukraine now involve multi-billion dollar oil deal tied to Trump & his allies
Article Text:
Lukoil oil deal enters US-Russia-Ukraine talks

Putin raised Lukoil deal with US negotiators

Who is seeking Lukoil’s assets

US approval remains crucial

Previous Lukoil bid stalled

Talks between the US and Russia over ending the war in Ukraine have expanded to include a proposed multibillion-dollar deal for Lukoil’s international oil assets, with the prospective investor group including people with business ties to US President Donald Trump’s allies. The deal would require approval from both the US government and the Kremlin.The proposed transaction covers Lukoil’s overseas portfolio of oil fields, refineries and gas stations. A group led by US investor Todd Boehly has emerged as the leading bidder, alongside Middle Eastern investors and the US government. The details were reported by The New York Times, citing eight people familiar with the negotiations.The negotiations have also brought renewed attention to the business links of Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who are leading US efforts to engage Moscow on the Ukraine war.There is no indication that Witkoff or Kushner would personally profit from the proposed transaction. However, the deal has raised questions about the overlap between the Trump administration’s diplomatic efforts with Russia and the business interests of people connected to the president and his allies.Russian President Vladimir Putin raised the proposed Lukoil transaction when he met Witkoff and Kushner at the Kremlin on September 5, according to people familiar with the meeting.Putin reportedly presented the deal as a potential way to demonstrate that Russian and US businesses could resume working together. The US side indicated it would work on the proposal, viewing it as a possible means of building goodwill with Moscow while potentially helping lower global energy prices.The proposed sale would also benefit buyers because US approval could release the assets from American sanctions, increasing their value.Lukoil’s international holdings include oil fields in Cameroon, refineries in Europe and gas stations in the US. While Lukoil is technically a private company, the decision over the deal is seen in Moscow as one that ultimately depends on Putin.Boehly, co-owner of the Los Angeles Dodgers, is leading the group currently seeking the assets. He donated $1 million to MAGA Inc. in December 2025 and another $1 million through his investment firm to Trump’s inauguration.The proposed investor group also includes Qatar-based businessmen Moutaz and Ramez Al-Khayyat and an Abu Dhabi investment fund controlled by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan.The Al-Khayyat brothers have business ties with Kushner and his wife, Ivanka Trump, including a planned luxury resort project in Albania.Sheikh Tahnoon controls an investment fund that acquired a significant stake in World Liberty Financial, the Trump family-linked cryptocurrency company co-founded by Witkoff. Trump’s sons are also involved in the company. Witkoff has since sold his stake, according to a person close to him.Sheikh Tahnoon also oversees Lunate, an Abu Dhabi investment fund that is among the major stakeholders in the private equity firm founded by Kushner after he left the White House.The Lukoil deal is not final and requires approval from the US treasury department, which oversees sanctions enforcement.The Trump administration had sanctioned Lukoil in October 2025 as part of measures targeting Russia’s energy sector and pressing Moscow over the Ukraine war.A senior US administration official said, as quoted by NYT, Witkoff and Kushner had directly participated in negotiating the financial terms of the proposed US government investment, including “a substantial upfront payment and profits interest for the United States.”The Lukoil assets have attracted several potential buyers since the company put its international holdings on the market.US private equity firm Carlyle reached a tentative agreement in January to acquire a large portion of the assets, but US approval for that bid stalled. The Boehly-led group subsequently emerged as the leading bidder.The treasury department has had to repeatedly extend sanctions-related arrangements while the sale remains unresolved. The latest extension is due to run until October 29.Lukoil valued its international assets at about $20 billion earlier this year, although the price and structure of the proposed transaction have not been disclosed.The proposed sale comes as the Trump administration seeks to use the prospect of renewed economic ties with Russia as part of its broader effort to persuade Moscow to compromise over Ukraine. Witkoff and Kushner have repeatedly travelled to Russia for talks with Putin as Washington pursues an end to the war.
Article Summary: Putin raised Lukoil deal with US negotiators at the Kremlin on September 5. Deal would require approval from both the US government and the Kremlin. A group led by US investor Todd Boehly has emerged as the leading bidder. Deal has raised questions about the overlap between the Trump administration’s diplomatic efforts with Russia and the business interests of people connected to the president.

Article Title: G7’s 100-million-barrel diesel fix: What happens after the emergency release
Article Text:
What happens after G7's emergency release

The replenishment challenge

How much is actually being added?

Supply routes under pressure

The G7 is tapping its emergency oil stash, with plans to release 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products to ease the diesel crunch. Earlier on Friday, the bloc said it would start opening the taps in the coming weeks, beginning with a “frontloaded substantial release” of diesel “immediately” and within the next 20 days. The remaining volumes will be released over four months.However, the strategy comes with its own share or risks and gaps.US President Donald Trump said that the diesel release would happen “immediately”, as fuel prices remain elevated across the US and Europe. The average US diesel price stood at $6.37 a gallon on Friday, according to AAA, after hitting a record $6.52 on September 22. In Europe too, diesel prices have reached record levels.France, which currently holds the rotating G7 presidency, announced the release after a videoconference led by President Emmanuel Macron, involving the G7 nations and EU representation. The move follows a March commitment by IEA members to release 426 million barrels, including around 92 million barrels from EU countries, largely refined products such as diesel, with Macron saying the latest release should add liquidity and lower prices.But the big question is whether the barrels coming out of emergency storage can keep pace with the pressures pushing prices higher.Russia has banned exports following Ukrainian drone strikes on its refineries, while refined fuel shipments from Persian Gulf producers have fallen because of war damage and blocked export routes.Though Europe does not import Russian diesel, countries such as Turkey and those in Latin America that buy it are now competing with Europe for the barrels still available.So, while the G7 is putting more fuel into the market, the squeeze on supplies has not necessarily disappeared. The emergency oil stash may offer some relief, but the supply problems behind the squeeze remain.The biggest risk identified by experts is what happens after the reserves have been used.Jim Krane, energy research fellow at Rice University's Baker Institute, told AP that the move could temporarily reduce retail fuel prices but would also leave Europe with less emergency cover.“Draining stocks will reduce retail fuel prices for a while, at the cost of leaving Europe with less emergency cover,” Krane said. “At some point in the future Europe and the rest of the G7 will have to refill their strategic reserves. Normally they try to do this when prices are low. Nobody knows when that will happen. It’s a risk.”That creates a second challenge for the strategy: the countries releasing the fuel will eventually have to rebuild their reserves, but the timing and cost of that replenishment are uncertain.Krane said the decision comes at a particularly uncertain point for energy markets, with two wars involving attacks on refineries and exports.With two wars raging that involve attacks on refineries and exports, “it’s not the best time to be frittering away your emergency stocks -- especially when there is no visibility on future prices or peace agreements,” Krane said.There is also uncertainty over the scale of the intervention.The G7's announcement comes after a March commitment by International Energy Agency member countries to release 426 million barrels of oil and products to stabilise the oil market. European Union countries had committed about 92 million barrels, with the release weighted towards refined products such as diesel.The G7 has now announced 100 million barrels, but it is unclear whether that figure represents an additional release or part of the earlier commitment.The lack of clarity limited the initial market reaction. US oil prices fell 2% following the G7 statement, but Pavel Molchanov, investment strategy analyst at Raymond James, said an important question remained unanswered.“The impact was lessened by lack of clarity on an important question,” Molchanov said.
